title: Sensor Modeling Research Toolkit
description: A research-grade Python toolkit for interpretable, probabilistic, privacy-preserving analysis of behavioural sensor data, and for multimodal ambient sensing in assisted-living and digital-health research. Alongside its established modelling core -- Bernoulli autoregressive models, hidden Markov models, change-point detection and non-homogeneous Poisson processes -- it provides an end-to-end pipeline from heterogeneous sensor observations to explained alerts: a canonical hardware-neutral observation model, online sensor-health estimation, probabilistic occupancy and person attribution from anonymous evidence, continuous-time multimodal fusion into latent behavioural states with explicit abstention, adaptive non-stationary personal baselines, restrained alerting, a synthetic household simulator with controlled ground truth, and a paired sensor-ablation framework. The design treats sensor failure, missing data, visitors and uncertainty as first-class modelling concerns rather than operational afterthoughts: a missing observation is never read as evidence of inactivity, and ambient activity is never automatically attributed to the monitored resident. No cameras, microphones or biometric identification are used anywhere in the design. This is research software and not a medical device; no claim of clinical effectiveness is made or supported.

notes: Research software. Not a medical device. Version 0.10.0 combines the Phase 3.1 time prior with the fitted hurdle channels in the filter's recursion, a pre-specified success on 20 public CASAS development homes, and confirms the time prior's gain once on 43 held-out CASAS homes. It offers that formulation in the online pipeline as an opt-in, off by default, with its parameters fitted once on the development homes. Tested once on ContextAct@A4H, one resident recorded independently of CASAS, the time prior's gain holds while the CASAS-fitted channels do not transfer. On the development homes, two activity sub-states are inconclusive, model-structure disagreement again ranks errors better than posterior confidence for the new formulation, and the abstention rule selected on it is not supported. The release also runs the pipeline on the TIHM clinical cohort, as an exploratory analysis, and adds opt-in silent-home and calibrated-baseline rules tested on simulated homes. Every experiment was pre-specified, with its protocol frozen before scoring. It does not change the online pipeline's defaults or the behavioural ontology. Figures from the bundled simulator remain simulator results and are not field-performance estimates.
